verses.1: In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah became king over Judah.
verses.2: He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Micaiah, the daughter of Uriel from Gibeon. There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
verses.3: Abijah mustered an army of four hundred thousand elite warriors, while Jeroboam arrayed against him eight hundred thousand elite warriors.
verses.4: Abijah stood up from Mount Zemaraim, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, and said, "Listen to me, Jeroboam and all Israel.
verses.5: Do you not know that the LORD God of Israel gave the kingship over Israel to David forever, to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?
verses.6: But Jeroboam son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon son of David, rose up in rebellion against his master.
verses.7: He gathered to himself wicked men, the sons of Belial, and they became strong against Rehoboam son of Solomon. Rehoboam was young and his heart was tender, and he did not strengthen himself against them.
verses.8: "And now you are saying, 'Let us rise up to face the kingdom of the LORD in the hand of the sons of David. You are a great multitude, and you have golden calves that Jeroboam made for you to be gods.'
verses.9: Have you cast out the priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and made for yourselves priests like the peoples of the lands, whoever comes to offer a bull or seven rams and becomes a priest of what is not a god?
verses.10: "But we, the LORD is our God, and we have not forsaken him. The priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron and the Levites, serve him in his work.
verses.11: They burn to the LORD an offering by fire, morning and evening, and the incense of spices, and the bread of the Presence on the clean table, and the golden lampstand and its lamps to be lit evening by evening, for we keep the watch of the LORD our God, but you have abandoned him.
verses.12: "And behold, the LORD is with us, and his priests and the trumpets to sound the alarm against you, O sons of Israel. Do not fight against the LORD, the God of your fathers, for you will not prosper."
verses.13: Then Jeroboam turned the ambush to come from behind them and placed them in front of Judah, while the ambush remained behind them.
verses.14: When Judah turned around, behold, they faced the battle from the front and the rear. They cried out to the LORD, and the priests sounded the trumpets.
verses.15: The men of Judah shouted, and when the men of Judah shouted, the LORD struck Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.
verses.16: The sons of Israel fled before Judah, and the LORD delivered them into their hands.
verses.17: Abijah and his people struck them with a great blow, and the slain among Israel were five hundred thousand choice warriors.
verses.18: At that time the sons of Israel were humbled, but the sons of Judah grew strong, for they had put their trust in the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
verses.19: Abijah pursued Jeroboam and took from him the cities: Bethel and its villages, Jeshanah and its villages, and Ephron and its villages.
verses.20: The strength of Jeroboam did not recover in the days of Abijah, and the LORD struck him and he died.
verses.21: Abijah grew strong, and he took fourteen wives for himself and had twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
verses.22: Now the rest of the acts of Abijah, and his ways, and what he said, are written in the annals of the prophet Iddo.
verses.23: Abijah lay down with his ancestors and was buried in the city of David. His son Asa became king in his place. During his time, the land had rest for ten years.

notes:
Notes
- v. 9: "the sons of Belial" is a Hebrew idiom for wicked or disorderly men; rendered as "the sons of Belial" to preserve the specific term.
- v. 15: "the men of Judah shouted" is a direct translation of the Hebrew, which uses the same root for both shouting and the divine action of shouting (the LORD striking).
- v. 21: "fourteen wives" reflects the Hebrew text, which counts fourteen wives, not a number that might be interpreted differently.
- v. 22: "annals of the prophet Iddo" is a fixed rendering for midrash, as per the glossary.
raw:
[1] In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah became king over Judah.

[2] He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Micaiah, the daughter of Uriel from Gibeon. There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.

[3] Abijah mustered an army of four hundred thousand elite warriors, while Jeroboam arrayed against him eight hundred thousand elite warriors.

[4] Abijah stood up from Mount Zemaraim, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, and said, "Listen to me, Jeroboam and all Israel.

[5] Do you not know that the LORD God of Israel gave the kingship over Israel to David forever, to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?

[6] But Jeroboam son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon son of David, rose up in rebellion against his master.

[7] He gathered to himself wicked men, the sons of Belial, and they became strong against Rehoboam son of Solomon. Rehoboam was young and his heart was tender, and he did not strengthen himself against them.

[8] "And now you are saying, 'Let us rise up to face the kingdom of the LORD in the hand of the sons of David. You are a great multitude, and you have golden calves that Jeroboam made for you to be gods.'

[9] Have you cast out the priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and made for yourselves priests like the peoples of the lands, whoever comes to offer a bull or seven rams and becomes a priest of what is not a god?

[10] "But we, the LORD is our God, and we have not forsaken him. The priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron and the Levites, serve him in his work.

[11] They burn to the LORD an offering by fire, morning and evening, and the incense of spices, and the bread of the Presence on the clean table, and the golden lampstand and its lamps to be lit evening by evening, for we keep the watch of the LORD our God, but you have abandoned him.

[12] "And behold, the LORD is with us, and his priests and the trumpets to sound the alarm against you, O sons of Israel. Do not fight against the LORD, the God of your fathers, for you will not prosper."

[13] Then Jeroboam turned the ambush to come from behind them and placed them in front of Judah, while the ambush remained behind them.

[14] When Judah turned around, behold, they faced the battle from the front and the rear. They cried out to the LORD, and the priests sounded the trumpets.

[15] The men of Judah shouted, and when the men of Judah shouted, the LORD struck Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.

[16] The sons of Israel fled before Judah, and the LORD delivered them into their hands.

[17] Abijah and his people struck them with a great blow, and the slain among Israel were five hundred thousand choice warriors.

[18] At that time the sons of Israel were humbled, but the sons of Judah grew strong, for they had put their trust in the LORD, the God of their ancestors.

[19] Abijah pursued Jeroboam and took from him the cities: Bethel and its villages, Jeshanah and its villages, and Ephron and its villages.

[20] The strength of Jeroboam did not recover in the days of Abijah, and the LORD struck him and he died.

[21] Abijah grew strong, and he took fourteen wives for himself and had twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.

[22] Now the rest of the acts of Abijah, and his ways, and what he said, are written in the annals of the prophet Iddo.

[23] Abijah lay down with his ancestors and was buried in the city of David. His son Asa became king in his place. During his time, the land had rest for ten years.

---
Notes
- v. 9: "the sons of Belial" is a Hebrew idiom for wicked or disorderly men; rendered as "the sons of Belial" to preserve the specific term.
- v. 15: "the men of Judah shouted" is a direct translation of the Hebrew, which uses the same root for both shouting and the divine action of shouting (the LORD striking).
- v. 21: "fourteen wives" reflects the Hebrew text, which counts fourteen wives, not a number that might be interpreted differently.
- v. 22: "annals of the prophet Iddo" is a fixed rendering for midrash, as per the glossary.
